blocks.para: Tap to click, twice to double-click. One tap is enough to open an icon in Program Manager.
For a right-click, either tap with two fingers, or press and hold still, then lift.
Two fingers scroll anything. On a page of text or a list, one finger scrolls it too, and a flick keeps going.
Pinch to magnify a window’s contents, then move about them with two fingers.
Drag a title bar to move a window. Swipe a menu bar sideways if it runs off the screen. A menu or a dialog too big to fit is dragged with one finger, anywhere on it.
Swipe in from the right edge to cycle through the open windows.
Swipe up from the bottom edge for the card switcher, then swipe across it to pick one.
Hold a title bar to bring up the keyboard, and hold it again to send it away.
Its top row adds the keys a phone has not got: Esc, Tab, arrows, Ctrl, Alt, Del, F1 to F10, Home, End, PgUp, PgDn and Ins.
In Tetris, Chip’s Challenge and the other keyboard games, a swipe is the arrow key it looks like and a double-tap drops. In JezzBall, the direction you swipe is the wall you get.
